subcategories.title: 1.1.1 General provisions
subcategories.text: ❗️This Regulation defines the terms and conditions for granting discounts upon admission to study under education contracts. It applies to bachelor's, specialist's, master's and secondary vocational education programmes. 🔍A discount is a percentage reduction in tuition fees. 📎Grounds: ✨ olympiads and intellectual competitions organised by the Financial University; ✨ results of entrance examinations; ✨ status as a graduate of the Financial University or a child of such a graduate; ✨ completion of additional educational programmes at the University; ✨ graduation from base schools, partner schools and partner colleges. ❗️Conditions: the discount is granted on only one ground (at the student's choice), is of a declarative nature, and requires timely payment. ✨ Suspension: during academic leave for medical reasons or military service (the discount is reinstated thereafter). ✨ Cancellation occurs in the event of a disciplinary sanction, academic leave (except for medical or military reasons), academic debts (score below 7️⃣0️⃣ or outstanding debt), or transfer to another programme, faculty or mode of study. ❗️The discount is non-transferable and is not retained upon expulsion or reinstatement. 📎Application and Cancellation ✨Application: submission of an application in the personal account and signing of an additional agreement to the contract (for higher education) or the contract itself (for secondary vocational education). ✨Cancellation: by order of the University or its branch. Exception: a discount granted by decision of the Rector. Amendments to these Regulations do not affect discounts previously granted. 💅 For more detailed information, please consult the full Regulation on Discounts.

subcategories.title: 1.1.2 Discounts for olympiad winners
subcategories.text: ❗️Discounts Based on Olympiad Achievements 📎For secondary school and college students: ✨ winner of level 1 — 1️⃣0️⃣0️⃣%, ✨ winner of level 2 — 5️⃣0️⃣%, ✨ winner oflevel 3 — 1️⃣0️⃣%; ✨ runner-up of level 1 — 5️⃣0️⃣%, ✨ runner-up of level 2 — 2️⃣5️⃣%, ✨ runner-up of level 3 — 5️⃣%. 📎For university students and graduates: ✨ winner of level 1 — 7️⃣5️⃣%, ✨ winner of level 2 — 5️⃣0️⃣%, ✨ winner of level 3 — 2️⃣0️⃣%; ✨ runner-up of level 1 — 5️⃣0️⃣%, ✨ runner-up of level 2 — 2️⃣5️⃣%, ✨ runner-up of level 3 — 1️⃣0️⃣%. Olympiad results are valid for 2️⃣ years. Discounts apply for the entire duration of study. ❗️For bachelor's and specialist's programmes, applicants must have a Unified State Examination score of at least 7️⃣5️⃣ in the relevant subject.

subcategories.title: 1.1.3 Discounts based on entrance examination results
subcategories.text: ❗️Discounts Based on Entrance Examination Results ✨ Bachelor's and specialist's programmes (Moscow): 3️⃣0️⃣–8️⃣0️⃣% depending on scores. ✨ Bachelor's and specialist's programmes (Branches): 1️⃣0️⃣–7️⃣0️⃣%. ✨ Master's programmes (Moscow): 2️⃣0️⃣–1️⃣0️⃣0️⃣%. ✨ Master's programmes (Branches): 1️⃣0️⃣–5️⃣0️⃣%. ✨ Secondary vocational education programmes: 1️⃣0️⃣–5️⃣0️⃣% depending on the average school certificate score.

subcategories.title: 1.1.4 Discounts for Alumni and Their Children & Graduates of Partner Institutions
subcategories.text: ❗️Discounts for Graduates and Their Children ✨ Graduate with honours (secondary general, secondary vocational or higher education) — 2️⃣0️⃣% for the first year. ✨ Graduate without honours — 1️⃣5️⃣% for the first year. ✨ Children of graduates — 1️⃣0️⃣% for the first year. ✨ Those who have completed additional educational programmes (at least 56 hours) — 1️⃣0️⃣% for the first year. 📎Discounts for Graduates of Partner Schools and Colleges ✨ Graduates of base schools of the Financial University and its branches — 1️⃣0️⃣% for the first year. ✨ Graduates of partner schools and colleges — 5️⃣% for the first year.

subcategories.title: 1.2.1 State academic scholarship
subcategories.text: ❗️State Academic Scholarship (SAS) 📎Mode of Study: full-time, state-funded. 📎Academic Performance: no academic debts and no grades of «satisfactory» in the most recent mid-term assessment. ❗️For students: 2️⃣4️⃣1️⃣9️⃣₽ per month. ✨ for those studying with grades of «good», «good» and «excellent» (as well as first-year students in the first semester); ✨ for international students studying within the quota (regardless of academic performance). 3️⃣6️⃣2️⃣9️⃣ ₽ per month. ✨ for students studying exclusively with «excellent» grades; ✨ for students from among orphans and children left without parental care; ✨ for students from among disabled children and disabled persons of groups I and II. ❗️«Gold of the Strong» Scholarship 4️⃣8️⃣3️⃣8️⃣ ₽ per month. ✨ paid in addition to the SAS for first-year bachelor's and specialist students in the first semester of their first year who are winners and prize-winners of the All-Russian School Olympiad, as well as winners and prize-winners of school olympiads included in the List of School Olympiads and their levels.

subcategories.title: 1.2.2 State social scholarship
1.2.3 Enhanced state academic scholarship (ESAS)
subcategories.text: ❗️Enhanced State Academic Scholarship (ESAS) 📎Amount: determined by multiplying the cost of one point by the total number of points earned by the student, and dividing the result by the number of months in the billing period. 🔍The cost of one point is determined by dividing the total funds allocated for ESAS payments in the billing period by the total number of points of all approved candidates. 📎Mode of Study: full-time, state-funded ✨When applying based on the winter examination session for a scholarship in the second semester: all years are eligible. ✨When applying based on the summer examination session for a scholarship in the first semester: all years except final-year students are eligible. 📎Academic Performance: no academic debts and no grades of "satisfactory" in the most recent mid-term assessment. 📎Criteria: achievements in academic, research, public, cultural, creative, and sports activities. 📎Application Procedure: Students of Moscow campuses enter their achievements electronically and submit an application in the Unified Personal Account at org.fa.ru.

subcategories.title: 1.2.4 Scholarship of the President of the Russian Federation
subcategories.text: ❗️Scholarship of the President of the Russian Federation 📎Amount: 3️⃣0️⃣ 0️⃣0️⃣0️⃣ ₽ per month for one academic year 📎Citizenship: Russian Federation 📎Mode of Study: full-time 📎Year of Study: 3–4 bachelor's, 3–5 specialist, 1 master's 📎Academic Performance: ✨ bachelor's/specialist students: ≥ 7️⃣5️⃣% «excellent» grades for the period, with no «satisfactory» grades or retakes ✨ master's students: honours degree diploma (≥ 7️⃣5️⃣% «excellent»), with no «satisfactory» grades or retakes 📎Achievements: victories in competitions, participation in R&D, publications, patents, targeted contract

subcategories.title: 1.2.5 Scholarship of the Government of the Russian Federation
subcategories.text: ❗️Scholarship of the Government of the Russian Federation 📎Amount: 2️⃣0️⃣ 0️⃣0️⃣0️⃣ ₽ per month for one academic year 📎Citizenship: Russian Federation 📎Mode of Study: full-time 📎Year of Study: 3–4 bachelor's, 3–5 specialist, 1 master's 📎Academic Performance: — bachelor's/specialist students: ≥ 5️⃣0️⃣% «excellent» grades for the period, with no «satisfactory» grades or retakes — master's students: degree diploma with ≥ 5️⃣0️⃣% «excellent» grades, with no «satisfactory» grades or retakes 📎Achievements: prize-winning placements in competitions, participation in R&D, publications, patents, awards, teaching experience

subcategories.title: 1.3 Enhanced State Academic Scholarship (ESAS)
subcategories.text: ❗️The Enhanced State Academic Scholarship (ESAS) 🔍It is awarded to full-time state-funded students of bachelor's, specialist, and master's programmes who have achievements in academic, research, public, cultural, creative, or sports activities. 📎Academic performance must meet the following requirements: no academic debts and no grades of "satisfactory" in the most recent mid-term assessment. ❗️When applying based on the winter examination session for a scholarship in the second semester, students of all years are eligible. ❗️When applying based on the summer examination session for a scholarship in the first semester, all years except final-year students are eligible. 📎The scholarship amount is calculated as follows: the cost of one point is multiplied by the total number of points earned by the student in the application, and the result is divided by the number of months in the academic period. 🔍The cost of one point depends on the total funds allocated for ESAS payments and the total number of points of all approved candidates. 📎Application procedure: achievements are entered electronically and submitted as an application in the Unified Personal Account (org.fa.ru portal). Path: My Resources — Documents — Scholarships — ESAS. ❗️Applications are accepted within the established deadlines, information about which is published on the Financial University website. 📎The number of candidates from a faculty must not exceed 1️⃣0️⃣ % of the number of students receiving the State Academic Scholarship based on the most recent assessment. Achievements for which a student has already received material or monetary rewards, as well as resubmitted achievements, are not taken into account. ❗️Payments are made monthly and are terminated in the event of academic debt, a bad grade, or a disciplinary sanction. 🔍Students on academic leave or maternity or childcare leave have their payments suspended for the duration of the leave and resumed upon their return. 🎅 Detailed information on deadlines and criteria is published on the Financial University website and in the faculty's official channels.

subcategories.title: 1.4 Academic leave
subcategories.text: ❗️General Provisions 🔍Academic leave is a temporary exemption from studies for valid reasons. 📎Grounds: medical indications, conscription or contract military service, exceptional circumstances (family reasons, emergencies, startup, study abroad, sports competitions, other valid reasons). 📎Duration: up to 1️⃣2️⃣ months (for medical reasons and military service — up to 2️⃣ years). The number of leaves is not limited. ❗️During leave the tuition fees are not charged, attendance is not permitted, academic scholarship is suspended (social scholarship is retained if eligibility remains). 📎Procedure for Granting Leave ✨ An application is submitted to the Student Office or through the personal account, along with supporting documents. ✨ For medical reasons and military service — the decision is made by the Vice-Rector within 2️⃣ working days. ✨ For exceptional circumstances — the decision is made by the faculty/branch commission within 5️⃣ working days. ✨ The decision is formalised by order, and the information is made available in the student's personal account. 📎Completion of Leave ✨ Upon expiration of the leave period or early — an application for readmission to studies is submitted. ✨ For early return from medical leave — a medical certificate is required. ✨ After the leave, an individual study plan is drawn up if necessary. ✨ If the programme is no longer offered — the student is transferred to another programme within the same faculty and field of study. ✨ A student who fails to resume studies after the leave is expelled. If return is not possible, the leave may be extended (application must be submitted 5 days before the end of the leave). 💅 For more detailed information about academic leave, please refer to the Academic Leave Regulations.

subcategories.title: 1.5 Disciplinary sanctions
subcategories.text: ❗️Disciplinary action at the university is based on respect for personal dignity. 📎For violations of the University Charter, Dormitory Regulations and other local acts, the following measures are applied: a reprimand, a severe reprimand, or expulsion. Only one disciplinary sanction may be imposed for a single offence. ❗️When choosing a sanction, the severity of the offence, the circumstances, the student's behaviour and state of health, as well as the opinion of student councils and parents, are taken into account. 📎No sanction is applied during illness, holidays, academic leave or maternity leave, nor to students with mental development delays or intellectual disabilities. ❗️Before a sanction is applied, the student must provide a written explanation within 3️⃣ days. 📎Refusal to provide an explanation does not prevent the application of a sanction. The sanction must be applied no later than one month from the date the offence was discovered and no later than six months from the date it was committed. 📎Expulsion of minors over 1️⃣5️⃣ years of age is permitted only in cases of repeated violations, provided that other measures have failed. 📎In the case of expulsion, the opinion of the relevant councils is taken into account; for students who have not received basic education, consent of the commission for minors' affairs is required; for orphans, consent of the guardianship authorities is required. ❗️The order imposing a sanction is communicated to the student and their parents within 3️⃣ academic days. The sanction may be appealed. 📎The duration of a sanction is 1️⃣ year. If no new sanction is imposed during this period, it is considered annulled. Early annulment is possible by decision of the Academic Council, upon the student's application, or at the request of the student council. No incentives are applied during the period of a sanction. The existence of a sanction is grounds for the cancellation of a tuition discount. 💅 For more detailed information, please refer to the Internal Regulations.

subcategories.title: 1.6.1 Reinstatement
subcategories.text: ❗️Reinstatement: 1️⃣For reinstatement on a state-funded basis, it is necessary to submit an application in the personal account on the website anketa.fa.ru. 2️⃣After the application is reviewed, the commission's decision will be reflected in the personal account. 3️⃣If the decision is positive, you must sign the reinstatement agreement in the personal account. 4️⃣After that, the order number and the study group number will appear in the personal account. 5️⃣Then you must contact the faculty — the class schedule will be available on the website ruz.fa.ru. ❗️For reinstatement on a fee-paying basis, you also need to submit an application in the personal account. The commission's decision will be reflected there as well. 📎Then you must sign a contract or additional agreement for reinstatement in the personal account. The payment receipt will appear in the personal account in the "Contracts" section. 📎After payment, you must attach the receipt in the personal account. 📎After that, the order number and the study group number will appear in the personal account. 📎Then you must contact the faculty — the class schedule is available on the website ruz.fa.ru. 💅 Detailed instructions and the required documents are available on the website: Transfers and Reinstatements.

subcategories.title: 1.6.2 Internal transfers within the university
subcategories.text: ❗️Documents for submitting an application for transfer: ✨ Application addressed to the Rector (in the prescribed form). ✨ Certificate of the period of study indicating the level of education, disciplines studied, practical training, and grades (not required for transfer within the Financial University from faculty to faculty). ✨ Certificate of foreign language proficiency (for programmes in English — after computer testing; for foreign nationals — certificate of Russian language proficiency). ✨ Other documents on achievements (optional). ✨ For foreign citizens — a copy of the identity and citizenship document. All documents must be translated into Russian and notarised. ❗️Transfer within the university: 1️⃣For transfer to a state-funded or fee-paying basis, it is necessary to submit an application in the personal account on the website anketa.fa.ru. 2️⃣After the application is reviewed, the commission's decision will be reflected in the personal account. 3️⃣If the decision is positive, you must sign the transfer agreement in the personal account. 4️⃣After that, the order number and the study group number will appear in the personal account. 5️⃣Then you must contact the faculty — the class schedule will be available on the website ruz.fa.ru. 📎For students on a fee-paying basis, it is additionally required to sign a contract or additional agreement for the transfer in the personal account. The payment receipt will also appear in the personal account in the "Contracts" section. 📎After payment, you must attach the receipt in the personal account. The order number and the study group number will be indicated there as well. 💅 Detailed instructions and the required documents are available on the website: Transfers and Reinstatements.

subcategories.title: 1.6.3 Transfers from another university
subcategories.text: ❗️Transfer from another university: 1️⃣For transfer from another university, it is necessary to submit an application in the personal account on the website anketa.fa.ru. 2️⃣After that, you must provide a certificate of the period of study. The commission's decision will be reflected in the personal account. 3️⃣If the decision is positive, a certificate of consent to the transfer will appear in the personal account, as well as a certificate from the Financial University, which must be sent to your university to obtain an order of expulsion in connection with the transfer. 4️⃣The received expulsion order must be attached in the personal account on the website anketa.fa.ru. 5️⃣You will also need to attach a certificate or diploma of previous education in the personal account. 6️⃣After all these steps, the transfer order will appear in the personal account. 📎For students on a fee-paying basis, payment is additionally required. The payment receipt will be available in the personal account in the Contracts section. 📎After payment, you must attach the receipt in the personal account. Then the transfer order will become available. 💅 Detailed instructions and the required documents are available on the website: Transfers and Reinstatements.

subcategories.title: 1.7 Exchange programs
subcategories.text: 🔍Inclusive Education is a long-term academic mobility programme under which a student completes part of their main educational programme at a partner university abroad through academic exchange. 📎Documents required for participation: ✨ Participant application form (in MS Word), endorsed by the Dean or the Head of the Master's programme. ✨ Transcript of records with the grade point average for the entire period of study. ✨ Original document certifying foreign language proficiency (international certificate or certificate from the Department of Foreign Languages). Duolingo is not accepted. ✨ Copy of the first page of the international passport. ✨ Additional documents: certificates, diplomas, confirmation of participation in conferences and olympiads (optional). ❗️An incomplete set of documents is grounds for rejection of the application. The application form must be coordinated with the Dean's Office. 💅 You may also refer to the methodological guide on Inclusive Education by the IER Student Council and the Inclusive Education website.

subcategories.title: 1.8.1 General ethical rules for all
subcategories.text: ❗️General ethical rules for everyone ✨ To remember the high status of the university and to bear with honour the title of its employee or student. ✨ To respect the traditions, history, and symbols of the Russian Federation and the university. ✨ Not to engage in activities that call into question the moral status of a member of the university community. ✨ To conscientiously comply with the charter, internal rules, and this Code. ✨ To always adhere to ethical norms and not to make thoughtless statements both within and outside the university. ✨ Not to allow discrimination against employees and students on any grounds. ✨ To show respect for the customs and traditions of representatives of different peoples. ✨ Not to conduct political, ideological, or religious agitation within the university walls. ✨ To observe a culture of behaviour, to show politeness, correctness, and goodwill. ✨ To be punctual and to comply with the access control system, working hours, and class schedules. ✨ To adhere to a business style in dress, characterised by restraint, strictness, elegance, and neatness. ✨ To observe a culture of speech, to address each other using the formal "You", not to use profanity, jargon, or slang. ✨ To observe ethical rules in social networks and online communities. ✨ Not to make value judgments in public speeches that could harm the business reputation of the university. ✨ To conduct work-related communication during working hours, not to send voice messages without prior agreement, and to avoid excessive use of smileys and emojis. ✨ To take care of property, maintain cleanliness, and use university resources economically. ✨ To provide support and assistance in the conduct of university-wide events and, if possible, to attend them. ✨ To arrive at events in advance, to turn off the sound on electronic devices, to observe the procedure and maintain silence, and to ask questions after the presentation. ✨ To exercise caution when communicating via third-party links and messages, and to use only official communication channels. 💅 For the full version of the Code of Ethics, see here.

subcategories.title: 1.8.2 Rules for staff and teaching staff
subcategories.text: ❗️Rules for employees ✨ To conscientiously perform labour duties, observe labour discipline and occupational safety requirements, and immediately report situations that threaten the life and health of people or the safety of property. ✨ To avoid actions related to personal or property interests that prevent the conscientious performance of duties. ✨ To carry out activities within the goals and objectives of their department and the university as a whole. ✨ To refrain from behaviour that may raise doubts about good faith or damage the reputation of the university. ✨ To refrain from negative statements about colleagues. ✨ Not to use official position for personal matters. ✨ To comply with the rules for providing official information and public speaking. ✨ To coordinate the topics of public speeches and comments for the media with the head responsible for information policy. ✨ To treat the work of media representatives with respect and to assist in obtaining reliable information. ✨ To take measures to ensure the security and confidentiality of information. ✨ To counteract corruption and take measures for its prevention. ✨ To demonstrate honesty and impartiality, and not to allow corrupt behaviour. ✨ Managers must be models of professionalism and impeccable reputation, contribute to the formation of a favourable climate, and prevent corruption manifestations among subordinates. ❗️Rules for teachers 📎All rules for employees apply to teachers. ❗️In addition, they are obliged to: ✨ To carry out activities at a high professional level and ensure the full implementation of educational programmes. ✨ To develop in students independence, creative abilities, civic engagement, and a culture of a healthy lifestyle. ✨ To take into account the psychophysical characteristics of students and their state of health. ✨ To be mentors and models of professionalism, and to contribute to the formation of a favourable climate in groups. ✨ To demonstrate objectivity and independence in assessing students' knowledge. ✨ Not to engage in commercial activities with students during working hours, including tutoring and the sale of educational literature.

subcategories.title: 1.8.3 Rules for students and appearance requirements
subcategories.text: ❗️Rules for students under the Code ✨ To strive to become a worthy specialist and professional in the chosen field. ✨ To show respect, politeness, and tolerance towards teachers, staff, and other students. ✨ To make decisions consciously and bear personal responsibility for one's actions. ✨ To demonstrate conscientiousness and activity in studies, to develop a creative approach and professional competencies. ✨ Not to allow dishonesty, deception, or fraud in the educational process. ✨ To exclude rudeness, humiliation of dignity, and profanity, and not to use the internet for familiarity. ✨ To respect others' intellectual property and to cite sources. ✨ Not to present others' work as one's own. ✨ Not to use personal connections or offer rewards to obtain a higher grade. ✨ To participate in student self-government and extracurricular activities. ✨ To show care for first-year students, to help international students and persons with disabilities adapt. ✨ To refrain from actions that detract from the honour and dignity of other students. ✨ To take care of the university's infrastructure. ✨ Not to participate in the organisation of unauthorised events on or off the university premises. ✨ To have an appearance that corresponds to the business dress code adopted at the university. ❗️Appearance requirements 📎The university has adopted a business dress code characterised by restraint, strictness, elegance, and neatness. ❗️ It is forbidden to wear tracksuits, jeans with tears and rips, shorts, and miniskirts. ❗️ It is forbidden to wear transparent and overly tight clothing, vests and tops with bare shoulders and deep necklines. ❗️ Sloppy and untidy appearance is forbidden. ❗️ Flashy and extravagant hairstyles with bright colouring are forbidden. ❗️ Flashy accessories and cosmetics are forbidden. ❗️ Sharp and overly strong perfume scents are forbidden; preference is given to light and unobtrusive fragrances. 📎Violation of the provisions of the Code is considered at meetings of collegiate governing bodies and the Ethics Commission. ✒️Compliance with the Code is taken into account during competitions for positions, certification, the application of disciplinary measures, as well as when considering matters of incentives for employees and students.

subcategories.title: 1.9 Summary of the Current academic performance regulations
1.9.1 General provisions
subcategories.text: ❗️The Regulation defines the procedure for ongoing monitoring and mid-term assessment of students in bachelor's, specialist, and master's programmes, as well as the elimination of academic debt. 📎Assessment is carried out according to the 1️⃣0️⃣0️⃣-point grading and rating system (GRS). 🔍Academic failure arises in the event of unsatisfactory results or failure to pass an assessment without a valid reason. 📎Students with academic debt are conditionally transferred to the next year of study and are obliged to eliminate it. ❗️A student has the right to retake a discipline no more than twice. If unsuccessful on the second retake — expulsion. 🔍The purpose of ongoing monitoring of academic performance is to check the level of competency mastery during the semester. 📎For bachelor's and specialist programmes (full-time and part-time), results are summed up twice: from 1 to 15 November and from 1 to 15 April. 📎The maximum score for ongoing monitoring is 4️⃣0️⃣ points (2️⃣0️⃣ points per stage). 📎The minimum threshold for assessment is 7️⃣ points out of 2️⃣0️⃣. ❗️With 6️⃣ points or less, the student is not assessed. Final assessment (pass/fail or exam) — 6️⃣0️⃣ points. 💅 For the full version of the Regulations, see here.

subcategories.title: 1.9.2 Mid-term assessment & Grading and rating system
subcategories.text: ❗️Mid-term assessment 📎Forms: pass/fail, pass/fail with grade, exam, defence of a course project, report on practical training. 📎A pass/fail grade may be awarded without questioning if the teacher agreed with that and if the results of ongoing monitoring are high (at least 3️⃣5️⃣ points out of 4️⃣0️⃣). The pass/fail is taken on the last day of classes. 📎The exam is conducted orally or in writing. The duration of a written exam is up to 2️⃣ academic hours; for an oral exam — preparation up to 2️⃣5️⃣ minutes, response up to 1️⃣2️⃣ minutes. ❗️Students with unauthorised materials or communication devices are removed from the exam with a grade of "unsatisfactory". 📎Provisions for students with disabilities Mid-term assessment is conducted taking into account individual characteristics. Upon application, the duration may be extended (written — up to +9️⃣0️⃣ minutes, oral — up to +2️⃣0️⃣ minutes). The presence of an assistant, special materials (Braille, large print), and sound amplification equipment is provided. The application must be submitted no later than 2️⃣ months before the assessment. 📎Grading and rating system (GRS) The 1️⃣0️⃣0️⃣-point scale is converted into grades: 8️⃣6️⃣–1️⃣0️⃣0️⃣ — «excellent», 7️⃣0️⃣–8️⃣5️⃣ — «good», 5️⃣0️⃣–6️⃣9️⃣ — «satisfactory», below 5️⃣0️⃣ — «unsatisfactory». 🔍A student rating is formed taking into account points and the credit load of disciplines. The student's place is determined based on the rating.

subcategories.title: 1.9.3 Appeals and elimination of academic debt
subcategories.text: ❗️Appeal 📎There are only 3 grounds for appeal: 1️⃣ the examination paper does not correspond to the programme, 2️⃣ incorrect wording of questions, 3️⃣ violation of the exam or pass/fail procedure. ❗️Dissatisfaction with the grade is not grounds for appeal. 📎The appeal is submitted on the day of the exam (if oral) or on the day the results are announced (if written). It is considered by a commission within 3️⃣ working days. The decision is final. ❗️Elimination of academic debt 📎Deadlines: for all except graduates — before the start of the next assessment period; for graduates — before the first state final assessment. ✨The first retake is conducted by the same teacher within the established deadlines. ✨The second retake is conducted by a departmental commission. The result is recorded in a protocol. Appeals against the second retake are not accepted. A student who fails to appear for the second retake without a valid reason is expelled.

subcategories.title: 1.9.4 Examinations and defense of course projects and papers
subcategories.text: ❗️Exams 📎Exams are conducted orally or in writing. 📎The duration of a written exam is up to 2️⃣ academic hours. 📎Preparation for an oral response — no more than 2️⃣5️⃣ minutes, response — up to 1️⃣2️⃣ minutes, additional questions — up to 1️⃣0️⃣ minutes. ❗️Results are announced on the day of the exam (for oral) or no later than the third day (for written). ❗️Regulations for the preparation and conduct of exams 📎The schedule is drawn up 3️⃣0️⃣ days in advance and communicated 7️⃣ days in advance. Changes — only with the permission of the Vice-Rector, published 2️⃣ days in advance. Examination papers are prepared on the basis of the approved structure and are delivered in sealed envelopes 1️⃣5️⃣ days in advance. ❗️Familiarisation with the examination papers before the exam is prohibited. Random selection of the examination paper is mandatory, as is the presentation of an identification document. In case of violations — removal. Results are announced on the day of the exam (for oral) or no later than the third day (for written). ❗️Defence of course projects and practice reports 📎Defence of the course project/paper is a mandatory stage. 📎The grade is given by the supervisor. The defence is conducted before the exam. ❗️A student who has not completed the work, has not appeared for the defence, or has received an «unsatisfactory» grade is considered to have academic debt. 📎Defence of the practice report is also mandatory. A student who has not completed the practice without a valid reason is expelled.

1.11 Transfer to state-funded education
subcategories.text: ❗️If you are studying on a fee-paying basis and wish to transfer to a state-funded place, you may submit an application to the Commission for the Transfer of Students from Fee-Paying to State-Funded Education or at the expense of the Financial University's own funds. 📎The decision is made subject to the availability of vacant state-funded places in your educational programme. 📎Who can apply? The right to transfer is granted to students who, at the time of application, have no academic debts, disciplinary sanctions, or tuition fee arrears. ❗️Conditions for transfer: 1️⃣ Excellent and good grades — if you have passed the most recent mid-term assessment with grades of «excellent» or «excellent» and «good». 2️⃣ Belonging to one of the following categories of citizens (except for foreign citizens, unless otherwise provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation): ✨ orphans and children left without parental care, as well as persons from among them; ✨ students under the age of 20 who have only one parent who is a group I disabled person, provided that the average per capita family income is below the subsistence level; ✨ women who gave birth to a child during the period of study; ✨ children of persons participating or having participated in the special military operation; ✨ participants of the special military operation (in the absence of academic debts, disciplinary sanctions, and tuition fee arrears). 3️⃣ Loss by the student during the period of study of one or both parents (legal guardians) or the sole parent. ❗️Important: the transfer is possible only if there are vacant state-funded places in your specialisation and mode of study. 💅 Meetings of the Commission are held within the timeframes established by Financial University Order No. 2195/o dated 02.10.2024.

subcategories.title: 4.5 Soft Skills Club
subcategories.text: Soft Skills Club is the first and largest student community in Russia focused on developing soft (interpersonal) competencies. It was founded in 2019 at the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation. Over the years, more than 2,000 students have been involved as residents, alumni, or participants in our educational and project activities. The club fosters a learning‑by‑doing environment and runs a variety of exclusive closed and open projects and courses. We visit top companies and invite renowned coaches, business trainers, executives, entrepreneurs, and experts who deliver free masterclasses, workshops, training sessions, and courses. Most importantly, at SSC you are not just an attendee – you can also create your own events, bringing your ideas and projects to life. The club is structured into 8 departments, each dedicated to a specific set of future‑ready skills: 1. Design – working with lines, colours, shapes, typography, and turning creative ideas into reality. 2. Media & PR – photography, copywriting, video editing, social media management, public relations, and promotion. 3. Psychology – learning to listen to yourself, understand and accept your emotions, and interact effectively with others. 4. Team Building – creating a warm and supportive atmosphere, finding common ground with diverse people, and building strong teams. 5. Leadership & Career – developing managerial qualities and mapping out your career trajectory. 6. Digital Skills – adapting and staying inspired in the fast‑paced world of technology, and applying soft skills in a digital environment. 7. Communications – honing interpersonal skills, public speaking, persuasion, and influencing others. 8. Thinking & Learning – cultivating critical thinking and self‑directed learning abilities. In addition, the club offers several special projects: · «Knizhnyy psikholog» – analysing books through the lens of psychology. · «Ledokol» – warm, welcoming events for having fun and making new friends. · «Tsifrovoy kompas» – using modern tools to boost digital literacy. · «Shkola Soroka» – a joint project of the "Media & PR" and "Design" departments, where top speakers help you master essential media and design skills. · «BEZVODY» – top employers and speakers share valuable advice and insights to help you build your career. Admission to the club is open year‑round. Large‑scale recruitment drives take place in autumn and spring, while individual applications are reviewed continuously throughout the year. To join an internship and eventually become a full‑fledged resident, you need to fill out a questionnaire, pass a personal interview, and complete an additional portfolio review (depending on the department you choose). Students from any year and any field of study at the Financial University are welcome – there are no restrictions. Contact information: If you have any questions about the club, the admission process, or upcoming events, feel free to reach out to us via direct messages in our VKontakte or Telegram communities (links below). subcategories.text: ❗️The International Students and Faculty Department provides comprehensive support to international students and staff, helping them adapt to the academic and social environment of the Financial University. 📎The main areas of activity include organising educational, cultural and social events, migration and visa support, developing the international environment and participating in preventive work. ❗️Contacts of the International Students and Faculty Department: ✨ Moscow, Leningradsky Prospekt, 51/1, room 0523, 5th floor. ✨ Office for International Students and Faculty: +7 (495) 249-53-00 (ext. 4951, 4952, 4954, 5319). ✨ Migration and Visa Office: +7 (495) 249-53-00 (ext. 6310, 6311, 6312). 📎The International Students and Faculty Department regularly organises events aimed at introducing students to Russian culture and legal system: Day of National Cultures, "Bridges of Friendship", the "Bridge to Russia" project, which includes legal adaptation of students, work with documents and electronic services, psychological training sessions jointly with the Psychological Service, off-site excursions, "The Russian Way", the ISFD Cup in various sports, as well as the Buddy System, which helps new students settle in more quickly. 💅 For more detailed information about the activities of the International Students and Faculty Department, please refer to the official website of the Financial University or the official Telegram channel.

subcategories.title: 5.4 Psychological Service of the Financial University
subcategories.text: 🔍The Psychological Service of the Financial University is free and anonymous psychological assistance for students and staff of all campuses. 📎What issues the specialists work with: ✨ Academic difficulties (exam anxiety, low motivation, procrastination); ✨ Personal and social problems (loneliness, conflicts, depressive states); ✨ Difficult emotional states (stress, burnout). 📎In what format are consultations held Consultations are conducted in person, online, or in writing via email. The duration of one session is 1️⃣ hour. ❗️Confidentiality is strictly observed, except in cases of threat to life and health. Specialists work on a voluntary basis, do not judge, and do not impose their own solutions. 📎How many consultations are available Students are entitled to up to 1️⃣0️⃣ free consultations during the academic year, staff — up to 3️⃣. In certain cases, an extension of the number of sessions is possible. 📎Contacts ✨ Appointments are available through the online form or by SMS to +7 (495) 249-53-00 (ext. 5198). ✨ The reception is located at: Moscow, 49 Leningradsky Prospekt, Room 104. ✨ Working hours: Monday — Thursday from 9️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ to 1️⃣8️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣, Friday — from 9️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ to 1️⃣6️⃣:4️⃣5️⃣. 💅 Detailed information is published on the Psychological Service page.

subcategories.title: 5.5 Military Training Center
subcategories.text:
🔍The Military Training Center at the Financial University is a structural unit where full-time students can undergo military training alongside their civilian education.

❗️Training is voluntary, based on a contract with the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation.

📎Training programs:

✨ reserve officers — 2.5 years (semesters 3–7);
✨reserve sergeants — 2 years (semesters 3–6).

📎Military occupational specialties:

✨ officers — MOS 030400, 030405, 030406, 097000 (Missile Forces and Artillery), 310101, 310201 (Financial Services of the RF Armed Forces);
✨ sergeants — MOS 140 (rocket artillery), 143 (mortars).

📎First-year bachelor's and second-year specialist's degree full-time students are eligible for selection.
Selection takes place from March to July and includes: submitting an application addressed to the rector, medical examination, professional aptitude testing, and passing physical fitness standards.
Students with Category 4 professional suitability are not admitted; those with Categories 2 and 3 go through two selection waves.

📎Classes are held one day a week (9 academic hours: 6 with an instructor, 3 of self-study). After the theoretical course — 30-day field training in July (for officers — in the 4th year, for sergeants — in the 3rd year). 

Upon successful completion, the rank of «Lieutenant» or «Sergeant» is awarded with enlistment in the reserves.

❗️How to get a deferment?

📎For Moscow students —
within the established deadlines, you must come to the Military Training Center with your passport, draft registration certificate, and SNILS; all further information will be sent electronically to the military enlistment office.

📎For non-resident students — you need to register with the Moscow military enlistment office to obtain a deferment and subsequently for admission to the Military Training Center.
You must provide your passport and draft registration certificate/military ID to the district military enlistment office. After registration, you can go to the Military Training Center and receive a deferment from conscription for the duration of your studies.

📎Contacts:
Address: Moscow, Kasatkina St., 15.
Phone: +7 (499) 270-22-62.

subcategories.text: ❗️ Places for 2026: For students admitted to the Financial University in 2026, 1️⃣0️⃣4️⃣3️⃣ places have been allocated in the dormitories. Of these, 10 places (5 rooms) are for student families, 31 places for persons with disabilities and limited health capacities, including 3 places for wheelchair users. 📎Priority order for providing accommodation: 1️⃣ Special priority (quota holders: persons with disabilities, orphans, combat veterans, participants in the Special Military Operation and their children, winners of olympiads) — based on the admission order. 2️⃣ Foreign nationals under the Ministry of Education and Science quota and fee-paying students who entered on a visa. 3️⃣ Dual-degree programs. 4️⃣ First-priority applicants (under Article 36 of Law No. 273-FL) — upon submission of supporting documents (in case of doubt, a request is made to the competent authorities). 5️⃣ General admission applicants — ranked in descending order of total competitive scores (Unified State Exam scores + individual achievements). For Master's and postgraduate students — ranked by entrance examination scores. Special conditions: Contract-target students, foreign nationals from visa-free countries (state-funded), and transfer students — are placed on a general basis in order of priority. Fee-paying foreign nationals from visa-free countries — are accommodated subject to availability. 📎The lists are published on the website within 5️⃣ days after the admission orders are issued. Move-in takes place one week before the start of classes. Those who fail to arrive without prior notice forfeit their place, which is then offered to the next person in line. 💅 Additional information and document templates can be found on the website page: Dormitories. ❗️ If you did not receive a place in the dormitory: ✨ Those who did not receive a place form a waiting list and are accommodated as places become available during the first year. ✨ When places become available — notification by phone/e-mail. ✨ The assignment is issued within 3️⃣ days upon submission of all documents. Move-in must take place within 3️⃣ days; otherwise, the assignment is cancelled.

subcategories.title: 6.3 Summary of the Student dormitory regulations
6.3.1 Procedure and priority for providing dormitory accommodation
subcategories.text: ❗️ Procedure for providing accommodation 📎The registration, lists, and assignments are managed by the Accommodation Services Office in coordination with the Vice-Rector. The basis for providing accommodation is an application; for applicants, it is automatically generated within the application form. 📎The number of available places is determined by the availability of vacant rooms, which typically become available after graduation, and is published on the website prior to the start of the admissions campaign. 📎The priority order for providing accommodation is as follows: 1️⃣ Special priority (quota holders: people with disabilities, orphans, combat veterans, participants in the Special Military Operation and their children, winners of olympiads) — based on the admission order. 2️⃣ Foreign nationals under the Ministry of Education and Science quota and fee-paying students who entered on a visa. 3️⃣ Dual-degree programs. 4️⃣ First-priority applicants (under Article 36 of Law No. 273-FL) — upon submission of supporting documents (in case of doubt, a request is made to the competent authorities). 5️⃣ General admission applicants — ranked in descending order of total competitive scores (Unified State Exam scores + individual achievements). For Master's and postgraduate students — ranked by entrance examination scores. Special conditions: Contract-target students, foreign nationals from visa-free countries (state-funded), and transfer students — are placed on a general basis in order of priority. Fee-paying foreign nationals from visa-free countries — are accommodated subject to availability. 📎Lists The lists are published on the website within 5️⃣ days after the admission orders are issued. Move-in takes place one week before the start of classes. Those who fail to arrive without prior notice forfeit their place, which is then offered to the next person in line. 📎Notification of available places — by phone/e-mail. The assignment is issued within 3 days, and move-in must take place within 3 days; otherwise, the assignment is cancelled. ❗️Accommodation is not provided to people who are registered in Moscow or the Moscow Region within a 50‑km radius; those who previously evicted for violations. 📎Students returning from academic leave (for medical reasons) who previously resided in the dormitories are accommodated as places become available. ❗️Information about the availability of places during the academic year is not published on the website.

subcategories.title: 6.3.2 Procedure for check-in
subcategories.text: ❗️Procedure for check-in 📎Check-in is carried out according to the approved lists or assignment from the Accommodation Services Office. ❗️For citizens of the Russian Federation, the following package of documents is required: ✨ passport with copies of pages 2️⃣, 3️⃣, and 5️⃣, ✨ medical certificate 0️⃣8️⃣6️⃣u with notes from a dermatologist and fluorography results, ✨ photograph 3️⃣×4️⃣, ✨ registration certificate or military ID, ✨ compulsory medical insurance policy (OMS), ✨ documents confirming benefits. ❗️For foreign citizens, the following are required: ✨ foreign passport with visa, ✨ migration card, ✨ photograph, ✨ voluntary medical insurance policy (DMS) valid for one year, ✨ medical certificate 086u or a comprehensive examination including fluorography, blood tests for RW, HBS, HCV, HIV, and malaria, as well as examinations by a therapist, dermatologist, and infectious disease specialist. ❗️For minors, the following are additionally required: ✨ written consent from a parent, ✨ copy of the parent's passport, ✨ copy of the birth certificate. 📎A tenancy agreement is concluded with the resident in two copies. All those checking in are familiarised with the internal rules against signature and undergo fire safety instruction. Registration at the place of residence is arranged through the dormitory's passport officer. 💅 For more detailed information, refer to the Regulations on the Student Dormitory.

subcategories.title: 6.3.3 Payment and eviction
subcategories.text: ❗️ Payment 📎Payment for accommodation is made monthly by the 1️⃣0️⃣th day of the current month. The amount of payment is established by order of the Rector, taking into account the opinion of the Student Council. ❗️The categories of citizens listed in Part 6 of Article 39 of Law No. 273-FZ are exempt from payment for hire, upon submission of supporting documents. The cost is recalculated when tariffs for housing and utility services and the rates of the Moscow Government change. 📎Eviction The dormitory is provided for the entire duration of studies. Upon expulsion or taking academic leave for reasons other than medical indications, it is necessary to settle all arrears and vacate the room within 3️⃣ calendar days, returning the premises and bedding. ❗️The possibility of residing during academic leave for medical indications is determined by decision of the Vice-Rector.

subcategories.title: 6.5 Summary of the Student dormitory Internal Rules Regulations
6.5.1 Procedure for check-in and access control
subcategories.text: ❗️ Procedure for check-in 📎Check-in is carried out according to the assignment from the Accommodation Services Office on the basis of a personal application. A tenancy agreement is concluded with the resident in 2️⃣ copies. Upon check-in, the resident is familiarised with the rules and given fire safety instruction. 📎Access control Entry to the dormitory is by campus cards through the access control system (ACS); transfer of the card to other persons is prohibited. Adult residents are granted round-the-clock access; minors — from 6️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ to 2️⃣2️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣. 📎Guests may be in the dormitory upon prior request from 9️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ to 2️⃣2️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣, with mandatory entry in the logbook. ❗️The bringing in and taking out of bulky items is registered with the duty officer; removal is carried out only with a material pass.

subcategories.title: 6.5.2 Rights and responsibilities of residents & liability for violations
subcategories.text: ❗️ Rights of residents: ✨ To reside in the dormitory for the entire duration of their studies, provided that the rules are observed. ✨ To use common areas, equipment, and inventory. ✨ To submit requests for repairs and troubleshooting. ✨ To participate in the work of the Student Council of the Dormitory. ❗️Responsibilities of residents: ✨ To use the living space for its intended purpose and to comply with the tenancy agreement and internal rules. ✨ To promptly submit documents for registration at the place of residence and for military records. ✨ To pay for accommodation and additional services on time, avoiding the accumulation of arrears. ✨ To observe quiet hours from 2️⃣2️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ to 7️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣, and to use appliances without disturbing the peace of other residents. ✨ To clean their room daily and to perform kitchen duties according to the established schedule. ✨ To compensate for any damage caused. ✨ To allow administration to inspect the room between 9️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣ and 2️⃣2️⃣:0️⃣0️⃣. ✨ To deposit duplicate keys with the duty officer for safekeeping. ❗️ Prohibited: ✨ To install additional locks and to store bulky items in rooms. ✨ To leave electrical appliances unattended while switched on. ✨ To bring in unauthorised persons and to provide one's place for others to reside. ✨ To appear in the dormitory under the influence of alcohol or drugs, and to store or consume alcohol and drugs. ✨ To smoke, including the use of vapes, as well as to use candles and aromatic products. ✨ To gamble. ✨ To move to another room without permission, to relocate inventory, or to independently repair the electrical network or plumbing. ✨ To keep animals and to use open flames. ✨ To damage walls, furniture, windows, and floors. ✨ To create noise, to throw rubbish out of windows, and to clog rubbish chutes. ✨ To conduct religious ceremonies in common areas. ✨ To humiliate the dignity of other residents and to cause them suffering. ❗️Liability for violations For violations of the rules, a warning, a reprimand, or expulsion may be applied, depending on the severity of the offence and previous conduct. Being under the influence of alcohol or drugs is an aggravating circumstance. 📎In the event of a violation, a report is drawn up and an order from the Vice-Rector is issued; expulsion is carried out by an order from the Rector. The violator is obliged to compensate for the damage. ❗️Eviction is possible for arrears exceeding 2️⃣ months, for damage to property, for systematic violations of neighbours' rights, or for absence of more than 3️⃣0️⃣ days without notice. 💅 For additional information, refer to the Internal Rules from the dormitory.

subcategories.title: 6.5.3 Dormitory administration
subcategories.text: ❗️ University responsibilities: ✨ To provide accommodation in the dormitory when available and to conclude tenancy agreements. ✨ To inform residents about the rules and to ensure registration at the place of residence. ✨ To furnish rooms with furniture, equipment, and bed linen. ✨ To carry out repair work, and to ensure the supply of heating, electricity, water, and other utility services. ✨ To ensure security of the dormitory, fire safety, and access control. 📎Head of the Dormitory The Head ensures check-in, conclusion of agreements, registration, and the changing of bed linen. He or she also controls payment, fixes malfunctions, and maintains order. 📎The Head has the right to relocate residents at their request, in cases of conflicts, or for technical reasons, and also to submit proposals for rewards and penalties. ❗️Student Council of the Dormitory The Student Council is formed from among the residents for self-governance. It coordinates the work of floor wardens and room leaders. The Council organises self-service, cultural and mass events, and also monitors the safety of property and compliance with discipline. 💅 Look for the group of your dormitory on VKontakte, or check information from activists in the dormitory chat.

subcategories.title: 7.2 Migration and Visa Office
subcategories.text: ❗️ Responsibilities and liability ❗️Compliance with migration rules is the obligation of international students. Violation entails a fine (Article 18.8 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation), deportation, and a ban on entry for up to 5 years. Registration at the actual address. 📎All foreign citizens must be registered strictly at the address of actual residence (Federal Law No. 163-FZ of 27 June 2018): ✨ In a private apartment — the owner is obliged to register you at the apartment address. ✨ In the Financial University dormitory — registration is arranged by the university (at the dormitory address). ✨ In a hotel — the administration is obliged to register you on the day of check-in for the entire duration of stay and issue an original with a stamp. After leaving the hotel, you have 3 calendar days to register at the new address. ❗️ Important: If you are registered at the dormitory but do not actually live there — this is a violation. The university is obliged to deregister you after 10 days of absence (except for trips and valid reasons). 📎Procedure upon entry and during the year: ✨ Each time upon entry into the Russian Federation, the previous migration card and registration become invalid. You must submit documents for registration anew. ✨ When crossing the border, check the accuracy of the data, the date of entry, and the purpose — «study». ✨ Report to the Migration and Visa Office within 2 working days from the date of crossing the border. ✨ If you have not left the Russian Federation during the year, report for extension of registration 30 days before the expiry of the current one. ❗️In case of loss or theft of passport, visa, migration card, or registration: 1️⃣ Immediately contact the police at the place of stay. 2️⃣ Obtain a certificate (notification slip) of loss — without it, stay in the Russian Federation is illegal. 3️⃣ Notify the Migration and Visa Office by any means. ❗️ Failure to contact the police in a timely manner is a violation of the law. 📎Contacts of the Migration and Visa Office ✨ Address: 51/1 Leningradsky Prospekt, Room 0209 ✨ Phone numbers: +7 499 553-12-15, +7 499 553-12-16 ✨ Email: ovu@fa.ru ❗️Important: The Office does not provide copying and printing services — copies of documents must be made in advance independently. When changing registration or address, you must send a photo or scan of the new registration form to the Office's email. 💅 For all current information, see the website of the Migration and Visa Office.

subcategories.title: 7.4 Russian Speaking Club
subcategories.text: ❗️ The Russian Speaking Club (RSC) is a space where you can freely practice conversational Russian, explore the culture and traditions of Russia, and make new friends among international students. 🔍The club meets several times a month, always in a lively and informal atmosphere: discussing films, books, current events, playing language games, and simply having conversations on interesting topics. 💜 Everyone is welcome at RSC, regardless of their Russian language level. The most important thing is the desire to speak, listen, and learn something new. The club helps not only to improve language skills but also to gain a deeper understanding of Russian culture from those who live it, as well as to find like-minded people from different countries. 📎To join the club and stay updated on all upcoming meetings and events, contact Arslan (@arrooox), who is the head of international student relations. He will add you to the group and share information about the nearest plans. 💗 Don't miss the chance to boost your Russian and expand your social circle!
